speaker: Doctor
text:
Can you describe exactly where the pain is located in your wrist or hand, and does it radiate to your fingers or elbow?  
Have you noticed any swelling, redness, or stiffness, particularly in the morning?  
REQUEST TEST: X-Ray of the right wrist.

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Patient
text: patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Gastroenteritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is very strange, as Gastroenteritis does not cause wrist pain or difficulty in hand movement; can you clarify if you experienced any nausea or vomiting before the pain started? Additionally, have you noticed any specific activities or injuries that might have triggered this, and when did the pain first begin? REQUEST TEST: MRI of the right wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal MRI and the previous confusion about gastroenteritis, I need to determine if this is an inflammatory, infectious, or mechanical issue. Have you experienced any recent fever, chills, or skin rash accompanying the wrist pain? Also, does moving your fingers or making a fist make the pain significantly worse?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Previous fall on right outstretched hand six months ago. No significant other medical history. Social history: Patient is a mother of an infant, leading a relatively active lifestyle. Does not smoke or consume alcohol regularly.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your history of falling on an outstretched hand six months ago, did you sustain a fracture or dislocation that might have healed incorrectly, and does the pain worsen specifically when you rotate your forearm? REQUEST IMAGES: Wrist X-ray (AP and lateral views).

speaker: Patient
text: Denies any fever, weight loss, or other joint problems.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Post-Traumatic Carpal Tunnel Syndrome.
